title: BIO 102 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER EIGHT ( WATER RELATIONS AND TRANSPORT IN PLANTS )
subject: BIO 102

questions.question: Water plays a crucial role in the life of which organism?
questions.explanation: Water plays a crucial role in the life of the plant.

questions.question: For every gram of organic matter made by a plant, approximately how much water is absorbed by the roots?
questions.explanation: For every gram of organic matter made, approximately 500g of water is absorbed by the roots.

questions.question: Even slight imbalances in the flow of water can cause water deficits and which issue?
questions.explanation: Even slight imbalances in water flow can cause water deficits and severe malfunctioning of many cellular processes.

questions.question: Every plant must delicately balance its uptake and loss of which substance?
questions.explanation: Every plant must delicately balance its uptake and loss of water.

questions.question: Balancing water uptake and loss is a serious challenge for which type of plants?
questions.explanation: This balancing is a serious challenge for land plants.

questions.question: Cytoplasm makes up what percentage of the cell volume in mature plant cells?
questions.explanation: In such cells the cytoplasm makes up only 5 to 10% of the cell volume.

questions.question: Water typically constitutes what percentage of the mass of growing plant tissues?
questions.explanation: Water typically constitutes 80 to 95% of the mass of growing plant tissues.

questions.question: Which plant part contains water at 35 to 75% and functions in transport in the xylem?
questions.explanation: Sapwood functions in transport in the xylem and contains 35 to 75% water.

questions.question: Seeds with a water content of 5 to 15% are among which type of plant tissues?
questions.explanation: Seeds with a water content of 5 to 15% are among the driest of plant tissues.

questions.question: Which structures can remain alive for long periods without water?
questions.explanation: Some structures like spores, seeds, cysts, and eggs can remain alive for long periods without water.

questions.question: Permenation refers to the ability of an organism to survive from one germination season to which point?
questions.explanation: Permenation is the ability to survive from one germination season to the next.

questions.question: Desiccation refers to the state or process of being which condition?
questions.explanation: Desiccation is the state or process of being desiccated.

questions.question: The cell wall of a plant is described as which characteristic?
questions.explanation: The cell wall of a plant is rigid and composed of several layers.

questions.question: The membrane that separates the cytoplasm from the cell wall is known as which structure?
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane separates the cytoplasm from the cell wall.

questions.question: The membrane found towards the vacuole is known by which term?
questions.explanation: The vacuole membrane is known as tonoplast.

questions.question: Both the plasmalemma and tonoplast are lipoproteins with which structural arrangement?
questions.explanation: Both membranes are lipoproteins with a bimolecular lipid center sandwiched between monolayers of protein.

questions.question: The cell wall of parenchymatous cells is composed of cellulose and which other substance?
questions.explanation: The cell wall of parenchymatous cells is composed of cellulose and peptide substances.

questions.question: Which process describes the passage of water through the cytoplasmic membrane?
questions.explanation: Water passes through the cytoplasmic membrane by osmosis.

questions.question: Osmosis involves the movement of solvent molecules from an area of high concentration to an area of which concentration?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of solvent molecules from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.

questions.question: A device that uses osmosis to power a flow of water out of a chamber is called which instrument?
questions.explanation: A device that uses osmosis to power a flow of water out of a chamber is called an osmotic pump.

questions.question: Which of the following is used as a differentially permeable membrane to demonstrate osmosis?
questions.explanation: Osmosis can be demonstrated using differentially permeable membranes such as a toad's bladder.

questions.question: In living tissues, osmosis can be demonstrated using which plant part?
questions.explanation: In living tissues, osmosis can be demonstrated using pealed yam or potato.

questions.question: Osmotic pressure is defined as the force that must be applied to stop which process?
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure is the force that must be applied to stop the osmotic movement of water across a membrane.

questions.question: An unsupported cell suspended in water due to high hydrostatic pressure undergoes which outcome?
questions.explanation: An unsupported cell suspended in water will burst like an over inflated balloon.

questions.question: Mesophyll cells have higher osmotic pressure values than epidermal cells because they have higher amounts of which substance?
questions.explanation: Mesophyll cells have higher values because they have higher sugar content.

questions.question: Which physiological process is controlled by osmosis?
questions.explanation: Absorption of water by root hairs from the soil is controlled by osmosis.

questions.question: The sieve theory of osmosis assumes that semi-permeable membranes have which feature?
questions.explanation: The sieve theory assumed that the semi-permeable membranes have pores.

questions.question: Which theory suggests that substances are soluble in the membrane itself?
questions.explanation: The solution theory is based on the assumption that substances are soluble in the membrane.

questions.question: The electrical theory of osmosis involves which type of gradient?
questions.explanation: The electrical theory suggests that an electrical potential gradient is developed.

questions.question: The presence of which structure allows plant cells to build up large internal hydrostatic pressures?
questions.explanation: The existence of the cell wall allows plant cells to build up large internal hydrostatic pressures.

questions.question: When a living plant cell is immersed in a strong hypertonic solution, the protoplast undergoes which change?
questions.explanation: The protoplast withdraws from the cell wall when placed in a hypertonic solution.

questions.question: Turgor pressure is demonstrated using strips of which plant part?
questions.explanation: Turgor in plant tissue can be demonstrated by using strips of potato petiole.

questions.question: Solutions that cause cells to swell or burst are said to be which type?
questions.explanation: Solutions that cause cells to swell, or even to burst, are said to be hypotonic.

questions.question: The continuous water column that extends through the plant is pulled from which part?
questions.explanation: The continuous water column that extends through the plant is pulled from the top.

questions.question: When transpiration from leaves is very low or absent, which phenomenon replaces passive absorption?
questions.explanation: When transpiration is very low, active absorption of water replaces passive absorption.

questions.question: The phenomenon caused by the continued active accumulation of ions by roots is known as which pressure?
questions.explanation: The phenomenon is called root pressure.

questions.question: Under certain circumstances, root pressure forces water to ooze out of a cut plant stem in a process known by which term?
questions.explanation: This takes place through a process known as guttation.

questions.question: The water that reaches the root xylem has to be directed upwards through which structure?
questions.explanation: Water has to be directed upwards through the xylem vessels of the stem, branches, and leaves.

questions.question: Bleeding from cut stems is due to the osmotic potential which operates in which part of the root?
questions.explanation: Bleeding is due to the osmotic potential which operates in the root cortex.

questions.question: The pressure generated by root pressure can raise water to a maximum height of approximately how many meters?
questions.explanation: The maximum height this pressure can raise water is about 10m.

questions.question: The cohesion-tension theory was put forward by Dixon and Joly in which year?
questions.explanation: In 1895, Dixon and Joly put forward their cohesion theory.

questions.question: The loss of water vapour by living plants through aerial parts is called which process?
questions.explanation: This type of water loss is called transpiration.

questions.question: Stomatal transpiration accounts for what percentage of total transpiration in plants?
questions.explanation: Stomatal transpiration accounts for 80-90% of the total transpiration.

questions.question: Which chemical is used on paper to demonstrate transpiration?
questions.explanation: The simplest experiment uses dry cobalt chloride paper.

questions.question: Which cells are described as the primary sensing organs of the stomata?
questions.explanation: The primary sensing organs of the stomata are the guard cells.

questions.question: In the measurement of loss of water, which substance is poured on the water surface to prevent evaporation?
questions.explanation: A little quantity of palm oil is poured on the water surface to prevent evaporation.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the rate of absorption by a cut shoot?
questions.explanation: The potometer is used to measure the rate of absorption by a cut shoot.

questions.question: Transpiration brings about cooling in plants as a result of the loss of which form of energy?
questions.explanation: It brings about cooling in plants as a result of the loss of the latent heat of vaporisation.

questions.question: Which of the following is an anatomical feature that helps reduce transpiration?
questions.explanation: Anatomical features include sunken stomata.

questions.question: Which environmental factor is considered the most important affecting transpiration?
questions.explanation: Light is the most important factor.
